profile_md: No qualifying scheme verified through the documented search. Caltech has no business school and the strongest team-project provision is engineering and computing based. ME 72 (compulsory design capstone for mechanical/civil engineering, teams of 5-7, two terms, robot competition 10 March 2026) meets project and group criteria but is an internal competition with no client. CS/IDS 163 Projects in Machine Learning is a group project course with 'domain expert advisors', whose affiliation is not stated. The 2026 Caltech Space Challenge is a selective five-day graduate team mission-design event with JPL (Caltech-managed) mentors and judges and no live client. E/ME/MedE 106 Design for Freedom from Disability is the only course with a named external partner (Rancho Los Amigos National Rehabilitation Center) but is not offered in 2025-26 or 2026-27 and team structure is not shown. The legacy SURF fellowship is mentored individual research, so it fails group working. Provision looks isolated and departmental; CALE offers careers services rather than team projects. Remaining uncertainty: unpublished sponsor roles in ME 72 and CS 163, and other departmental project courses not individually checked.
gaps: Reduced-depth review (about 12 searches). Not checked: whether ME 72 sponsors (Northrop Grumman per a search snippet) set briefs; CS/IDS 163 advisor identity; CS 141 partners; JPL-linked courses; engineering EE/CMS project courses (e.g. CS/EE 145); Applied Physics/Materials design courses; further departmental instances likely.
